The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team** represented **Harvard University** during the **2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season**. Coached by **Tommy Amaker** in his fifth season, the team had a historic season, winning the **Ivy League** for the first time since 1946 and earning the program's first-ever **NCAA Tournament bid**. Here’s everything you need to know about that team:

---

### **Key Facts & Achievements**
- **Record**: **26–5** (12–2 Ivy League) – **Ivy League Champions**
- **NCAA Tournament**: **#12 seed** in the **West Region** (lost to #5 Vanderbilt in the First Round)
- **Firsts for Harvard Basketball**:
  - First **Ivy League title** in 66 years (since 1946).
  - First **NCAA Tournament appearance** in program history.
  - First **20-win season** since 1945–46.
  - First **AP Top 25 ranking** (peaked at **#22** in February 2012).
- **Coach**: **Tommy Amaker** (5th season at Harvard, former Duke player and Michigan coach).
- **Home Court**: **Lavietes Pavilion** (capacity: 2,195).

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The 2011–12 team was led by a talented core of upperclassmen, including:

#### **Starters & Key Contributors**
| **Player**          | **Position** | **Year** | **Key Stats (2011–12)** | **Notes** |
|---------------------|-------------|----------|------------------------|-----------|
| **Keith Wright**    | PF/C        | Senior   | 10.9 PPG, 8.1 RPG, 1.5 BPG | **Ivy League Player of the Year** (2011), two-time First-Team All-Ivy. |
| **Oliver McNally**  | SG          | Senior   | 10.1 PPG, 3.5 APG, 41% 3PT | Team captain, clutch shooter, hit the **game-winning shot** vs. Princeton (2011). |
| **Kyle Casey**      | PF          | Junior   | 11.3 PPG, 5.5 RPG, 1.1 SPG | **First-Team All-Ivy**, explosive athlete, later played professionally in Europe. |
| **Brandyn Curry**   | PG          | Junior   | 7.2 PPG, 4.9 APG, 1.7 SPG | **First-Team All-Ivy**, elite passer and defender. |
| **Christian Webster** | SG      | Junior   | 8.5 PPG, 40% 3PT | Sharpshooter, key bench scorer. |
| **Laurent Rivard**  | SG          | Sophomore| 6.0 PPG, 42% 3PT | Emerging shooter, later became a star. |
| **Steve Moundou-Missi** | PF/C | Freshman | 3.5 PPG, 2.8 RPG | Future starter, defensive anchor. |

#### **Bench & Role Players**
- **Jonah Travis** (Fr) – Future starter, energy big man.
- **Matt Brown** (Sr) – Role player, defensive specialist.
- **Ugo Okam** (Sr) – Backup center, shot-blocker.
- **Corbin Miller** (Fr) – Shooter, redshirted this season.

---

### **Season Highlights & Key Games**
#### **Non-Conference Play (14–1 Record)**
- **Nov. 11, 2011**: **Harvard 66, MIT 53** – Season opener.
- **Nov. 21, 2011**: **Harvard 67, Florida State 48** – **Upset win** over a **#22-ranked** Seminoles team (later a Sweet 16 team).
- **Dec. 5, 2011**: **Harvard 64, Boston College 61** – **Road win** over ACC foe BC.
- **Dec. 19, 2011**: **Harvard 80, George Washington 67** – **First AP Top 25 ranking** (#25) in program history.
- **Dec. 29, 2011**: **Harvard 87, St. Joseph’s 84 (OT)** – **Neutral-court win** in the **Hawk Classic**.
- **Jan. 7, 2012**: **Harvard 69, Boston University 53** – **20th win** of the season (first 20-win season since 1946).

#### **Ivy League Play (12–2 Record)**
Harvard entered the Ivy League season as the **favorite** after finishing **10–4** the previous year (tied for 2nd). They dominated most of the league but had **two close losses** to **Princeton** and **Yale**.

- **Jan. 20, 2012**: **Harvard 65, Dartmouth 56** – Ivy opener.
- **Feb. 3, 2012**: **Harvard 59, Princeton 57** – **Key home win** over rival Princeton (later shared the Ivy title).
- **Feb. 10, 2012**: **Yale 70, Harvard 69** – **Upset loss** at Yale (Harvard’s only Ivy road loss).
- **Feb. 24, 2012**: **Harvard 69, Columbia 59** – **Clinched at least a share of the Ivy title**.
- **Mar. 3, 2012**: **Harvard 70, Cornell 61** – **Outright Ivy League championship** (first since 1946).

#### **NCAA Tournament (First Round Exit)**
- **Selection Sunday (Mar. 11, 2012)**: Harvard earned a **#12 seed** in the **West Region**, facing **#5 Vanderbilt**.
- **Mar. 15, 2012**: **Vanderbilt 79, Harvard 70** (Albuquerque, NM)
  - Harvard led **35–34 at halftime** but faded in the second half.
  - **Keith Wright** had **18 points & 9 rebounds**, but Vanderbilt’s **John Jenkins** (27 pts) and **Jeffery Taylor** (15 pts) took over.
  - **Final Ivy League record**: **12–2** (tied with Princeton, but Harvard won the head-to-head tiebreaker).

---

### **Awards & Honors**
- **Tommy Amaker** – **Ivy League Coach of the Year**
- **Keith Wright** – **Ivy League Player of the Year**, **First-Team All-Ivy**, **Academic All-American**
- **Kyle Casey** – **First-Team All-Ivy**
- **Brandyn Curry** – **First-Team All-Ivy**
- **Oliver McNally** – **Second-Team All-Ivy**
- **Team** – **AP Top 25 (#22 peak)**, **NCAA Tournament appearance**

---

### **Legacy & Impact**
- **Program-Changing Season**: This team **put Harvard basketball on the map**, leading to future NCAA Tournament appearances (2013, 2014, 2015).
- **Recruiting Boost**: The success helped Amaker recruit **higher-caliber players**, including **Wesley Saunders** (future Ivy POY) and **Siyani Chambers**.
- **Academic & Athletic Balance**: The team was known for its **high graduation rates** and **student-athlete excellence** (multiple Academic All-Ivy selections).
- **Princeton Rivalry**: This season intensified the **Harvard-Princeton rivalry**, which became the Ivy League’s best in the 2010s.

---

### **Where Are They Now?**
| **Player**          | **Post-Harvard Career** |
|---------------------|------------------------|
| **Keith Wright**    | Played professionally in **Europe (France, Germany, Israel)**; later became a **coach** (assistant at Harvard, then head coach at **St. Mary’s HS (CA)**). |
| **Oliver McNally**  | Played professionally in **Germany**; later worked in **finance** (Goldman Sachs). |
| **Kyle Casey**      | Played professionally in **Europe (Spain, Germany, Israel)**; later became a **real estate developer**. |
| **Brandyn Curry**   | Played professionally in **Europe (Germany, Netherlands)**; later became a **high school coach** (New Jersey). |
| **Christian Webster** | Played professionally in **Europe (Germany, Finland)**; later worked in **tech**. |
| **Laurent Rivard**  | Played professionally in **Europe (France, Germany)**; later became a **financial analyst**. |
| **Steve Moundou-Missi** | Played professionally in **Europe (France, Germany, Switzerland)**; later worked in **business**. |

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- **First NCAA Tournament Win?** Harvard’s first **NCAA Tournament win** came the **next year (2013)**, when they beat **New Mexico** as a **#14 seed**.
- **Jeremy Lin Connection**: This team played **before Jeremy Lin’s NBA fame**, but Lin (Class of 2010) was a key part of the **2009–10 and 2010–11** teams that laid the foundation.
- **Lavietes Pavilion Upgrades**: The success led to **renovations** of Lavietes Pavilion (completed in 2013).
- **ESPN’s "30 for 30" Potential**: The 2011–12 team’s story was so compelling that it was **considered for a documentary** (though none was made).
- **Academic Success**: **100% graduation rate** for the team, with multiple players earning **Rhodes Scholarship nominations**.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
The **2011–12 Harvard Crimson** were a **historic team** that **ended a 66-year Ivy League title drought** and **brought Harvard basketball into the national spotlight**. While they fell short in the NCAA Tournament, their **26-win season**, **AP Top 25 ranking**, and **first-ever March Madness bid** set the stage for Harvard’s **golden era** in the 2010s.
